(2)  The  Commissioner-General  may  specify  the

column1: circumstances in which the replacement of one security in a
company with another security in the same company or a
different company (including as a result of merger, demerger
or reconstruction) constitutes an involuntary realisation.

column2: (1) Subject to section 49 where rights or obligations

column1: with respect to an asset owned by one person are assigned to
another person, including by way of lease of an asset or part

column2: where the rights or obligations are permanent, the
one person shall  be treated as realising part of the
asset, but shall not be treated as acquiring any new
asset or liability; and
where  the  rights  or  obligations  are  temporary  or
contingent,  the  person  shall  not  be  treated  as
realising  part  of  the  asset  or  liability,  but  as
acquiring a new asset or incurring a new liability,
as the case requires.
(2) Rights or obligations shall be considered permanent

column1: when they are likely to last for more than fifty years.

column2: (1)  Where  a  person  grants  a  mortgage  (legal  or

column1: equitable) or similar form of security over an asset to secure
a debt owed to another person –

column2: the first person shall not be treated as realising the
asset or any part of it, but shall be treated as still
owning the asset and as having incurred a liability
being the secured debt; and
the other person shall not be treated as acquiring
the asset or any part of it, but shall be treated only
as owning the secured debt.
(2)  Where  an  asset  is  leased  under  a  finance  lease,  the

column1: lessor shall be treated as transferring ownership of the asset
